cands.name: Pia Dandiya
cands.bio: Democratic nominee. Began as a teacher, became a Harlem high-school principal, served as a White House Fellow at the Education Department, then led public-sector work at Apple. Born and raised in Palm Beach County to parents from India. Has not held office. Originally ran against Brian Mast in CD 21, switched to the new open CD 22.
cands.local_ties: Raised in Palm Beach County; campaign mailing address in Royal Palm Beach.

record.text: Switched from the CD 21 race to open CD 22 after the 2026 map change (Florida Politics, May 22, 2026).
Priorities: lower costs (housing, insurance), end tariffs and restore ACA subsidies, protect Social Security and Medicare, stand up to corruption.

money_notes.text: As of May 2026 she had raised $1.575 million and loaned her campaign $197,000 (FEC figures cited by Floridian Press).
House Majority PAC reportedly bought about $9.7 million in ads supporting her and attacking Askar (Floridian Press; page did not load).

Republican-aligned Stronger America Together PAC attacked her over investments disclosed in her House financial disclosure (H.I.G. Capital, which acquired a data center operator; net worth listed at $9-11 million).

controversies.text: Mailer by Stronger America Together PAC calls her a 'hypocrite' for criticizing data centers while holding investments tied to one; its website also alleges an investment in a Chinese government-owned hedge fund (not verified).

endorsements.text: DCCC Red to Blue, EMILY's List, Florida AFL-CIO, Florida Democratic Party chair Nikki Fried, Sun Sentinel editorial board (primary), Rep. Jason Crow, DNC chair Ken Martin, Democratic Majority for Israel, JDCA, LCV Action Fund (as listed on Wikipedia).

cands.gaps: No photo found. A search summary said she was a registered Republican until 2020 (Florida Politics launch coverage); I could not open that article, so it is not stated as fact. Owner-source search surfaced only unrelated 'dandiya' dance pages.

cands.name: Casey Askar
cands.bio: Republican nominee. Chairman and CEO of Askar Family Office (franchising, commercial real estate, energy, construction). Iraqi-born Marine veteran (1988-1992) who came to the U.S. at age 7. Never held office; lost the 2020 District 19 GOP primary to Byron Donalds. Won the 2026 District 22 primary with about 31%.
cands.local_ties: Naples/Collier County businessman (Passidomo and Sheriff Rambosk endorsed him as a local); the new District 22 spans inland Palm Beach and Broward (Wellington, Parkland), all of rural Hendry County and southern Collier County including Marco Island.

record.text: Says he operates businesses in about two dozen states and employs 2,000 people in the district and South Florida; wants an Appropriations seat; praised Trump's removal of Maduro and called for ending communist rule in Venezuela and Cuba.
Website platform: cut taxes, 'ensure that only American citizens can vote'. Did not respond to WGCU's requests for comment.

money_notes.text: Loaned his campaign about $2.5 million during the primary (as stated on a Club for Growth page that backed rival Carbonara; I did not verify against FEC).
House Majority PAC reportedly bought about $9.7 million in ads supporting Pia Dandiya and mainly attacking Askar (Floridian Press, Oct 7, 2026; headline seen, article page did not load).

An HMP-attributed mailer calls him a 'Corrupt Businessman' worth about $636 million; Floridian Press noted his disclosure suggests closer to $400 million and found no evidence on his site that he backs tax increases.

controversies.text: Democratic-aligned mailer alleges 'shady business practices'; no specific wrongdoing documented in the article.

endorsements.text: Donald Trump (WLRN, Sept 3, 2026), Gov. DeSantis, NRCC MAGA Majority (Wikipedia); in the primary: Rep. Gus Bilirakis, Collier Sheriff Kevin Rambosk, Kathleen Passidomo, CPAC, Michael Flynn.

cands.gaps: Residence not confirmed in opened sources. A 2020 lawsuit he filed against Byron Donalds ($30,000 defamation) appeared in search results but I did not open it, so it is not listed. Trump endorsement rests on a WLRN headline and Wikipedia; the article text was not read.
